exposure: onset of wheezing in the first trimester of life
cohort: The study included 2,079 infants aged 12-18 months with recurrent asthma-like symptoms from 11 South American centres.
finding: The prevalence of admission for wheezing was 29.7%, significantly associated with factors like severe wheezing episodes, physician-diagnosed asthma, maternal tobacco smoking during pregnancy, and early wheezing onset, while breastfeeding, higher maternal education, and higher household income were protective.
